newsitem.title: USA: Wis. Wal-Mart workers first in U.S. to consider union.
newsitem.headline: Wis. Wal-Mart workers first in U.S. to consider union.

text.p: Workers at a Wal-Mart store in northern Wisconsin were set to vote Friday on whether to join the United Steelworkers of America, the first time Wal-Mart employees in the United States have considered unionizing, company and union officials said.
Some 90 of the 120 part- and full-time workers at the Wal-Mart Stores Inc. outlet in Merrill, Wis., were eligible to vote.
"We have a petition from the steelworkers, who are wanting to represent our associates in the store only in Merrill," said Betsy Reithemeyer, senior manager of corporate affairs for Wal-Mart Stores.
Of Wal-Mart's 780,000 employees worldwide, 70 percent are full-time, and only workers at the Wal-Mart store in Windsor, Ontario, Canada, belong to a union, she added.
Results of the Merrill store's vote, which was being conducted by the National Labour Relations Board, were expected Friday night.
"The federal law is ... if there were 90 (voters) you need 46" to approve the petition, said Bob Glaser of the United Steelworkers of America in Milwaukee.
"The issues are wages, equity and other problems," said Patsy Schafer, staff representative for District Two of the Steelworkers union.

Although votes to unionize have occurred at Wal-Mart affiliates, including the warehouse-like Sam's Club, none has occurred at a U.S. Wal-Mart, Reithemeyer said. -- ((Reuters Chicago Newsdesk (312) 408-8787))
